title: Eggoz onboards Boman Irani as brand ambassador
raw_summary:
On October 6, 2027, Eggoz, India's first egg brand focused on clean, traceable, and high-protein nutrition, announced the onboarding of acclaimed actor Boman Irani as its brand ambassador, along with a new campaign to mark the association. It's a happy match. Both the brand and the man have the same easy knack for winning people over with warmth, wit and a wink. Boman's versatile screen presence, sharp comic timing and gift for finding the funny in everyday moments make him a natural fit for a brand that wants good food, good nutrition and a good time to be part of your daily plate.

The campaign, conceptualised by ANC, puts Boman right at the centre of the fun and takes a fresh, playful route to the simple joy of eating an Eggoz egg. It all unfolds in a sleepy office where nothing ever moves fast, until Boman, the classic office boss, strolls in fresh from lunch and sets off a chain reaction of impossibly quick, joyful chaos. Files fly, stamps thump, and stunned faces melt into delight, all thanks to what the campaign calls the "Eggoz effect." The secret, revealed over a spread of golden bhurji, fluffy omelettes and sunny side ups with rich orange yolks, is simple: Eggoz doesn't just fill you up, it fires you up. A cheerful little reminder that food isn't only fuel, it's colour, flavour and everyday joy on a plate.

Speaking on the association, Abhishek Negi, Co-founder and CEO, Eggoz, said, "Boman Irani brings a warmth and humour that instantly connects with people, which is exactly what Eggoz stands for. We've always believed that a good egg can change the mood of an entire meal, and this campaign captures that spirit with a lot of heart and a lot of fun. Having Boman embody the 'Eggoz effect' felt like the most natural way to tell our story."

Commenting on the partnership, Boman Irani said, "What drew me to Eggoz is how they've taken something as everyday as an egg and made it feel special. The film was a joy to shoot because it doesn't take itself too seriously, and yet it says something true, that the little things on your plate can genuinely brighten your day. I had a wonderful time being part of it."

Adding to this, Shivan Nair, Head of Marketing, Eggoz, said, "For us, this campaign was about making the everyday egg impossible to ignore. Boman brings a warmth and humour that cuts through instantly, and that's exactly the kind of connection we wanted with our consumers. The 'Eggoz effect' is really our brand promise in disguise, that good food should lift your whole day, and we can't wait for audiences to see it come alive."

Adding to this, Samarjeet Shimpi, CEO, ANC said, "The brand needed to own an emotion in the egg space. We defined Eggoz as being delightful and full of energy. Hence, the expression, Sunny Side Up. Boman exemplifies it the best."

The campaign reflects Eggoz's larger belief that quality food should be an integral, enjoyable part of everyday life. With freshly dispatched eggs from hens on a special herbal diet, rigorous quality standards and a distinctive rich orange yolk, Eggoz continues to build a brand that pairs nutrition with genuine everyday joy, turning even the most mundane moments sunny side up.

title: Sonu Nigam expands Mumbai property portfolio, buys commercial units in Andheri West for Rs. 16 crores
raw_summary:
Playback singer Sonu Nigam has expanded his real estate portfolio with the acquisition of multiple commercial units in Andheri West, Mumbai. According to property registration documents accessed by real estate data analytics platform CRE Matrix, Nigam has invested a total of over Rs. 16 crores in three office units located in the Aston commercial tower at Sundervan Complex on Lokhandwala Road.

The primary transaction involves two adjoining office spaces situated on the first floor of the building. The properties have a combined carpet area of 3,885.77 sq. ft and were acquired from Singular Health Private Limited for a total consideration of Rs. 16 crores. The transaction translates to an approximate rate of Rs. 41,175.88 per sq. ft. Stamp duty of Rs. 96 lakhs were paid as part of the registration.

The two office units also come with dedicated access to four car parking spaces in the basement stack-parking system of the building.

In a separate transaction registered during the same cycle, Nigam acquired another commercial unit in the same Aston building from the same seller. The ground-floor office measures 258.33 sq. ft and was purchased for Rs. 1 crore. The transaction attracted a stamp duty of Rs. 6 lakhs.

With the latest acquisition, Sonu Nigam’s total holding in the Aston property now covers 4,144.10 sq. ft of carpet area. His combined investment across the three units stands at Rs. 17 crores, translating to an average acquisition rate of approximately Rs. 41,021 per sq. ft.

The latest purchase adds to the singer’s real estate activity across Mumbai and Maharashtra over the past two years. In late 2025, Nigam leased a 4,257 sq. ft commercial office at Trade Centre BKC in Santacruz East to Pattni Hospitality, operators of the café-bar chain Downtown 29. The five-year lease is expected to generate more than Rs. 12.61 crores in cumulative rental income over its tenure.

Nigam has also undertaken transactions involving land holdings in Karjat. In April 2026, he sold multiple land parcels in Raigad district measuring more than 1.9 hectares for Rs. 1.95 crores. A separate 1.067-hectare land parcel was sold in May 2026 for Rs. 95 lakhs.

Meanwhile, his father Agam Kumar Nigam acquired a 1,197 sq. m. land parcel in Madh Island in February 2026. The property includes a ground-plus-one residential and commercial structure and was purchased for Rs. 10 crores.

With Andheri West serving as an established commercial hub for businesses associated with Mumbai’s media and entertainment ecosystem, Sonu Nigam’s latest acquisition adds to the growing interest among Bollywood personalities in commercial real estate across Mumbai’s suburban corridors.

title: Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha producer Prakash Mahobiya alleges ‘negative marketing’; hints at big-budget Ramayana saying, “We never got a chance to reach our audience”
raw_summary:
Producer Prakash Mahobiya has opened up about the theatrical performance of Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha, alleging that the mythological drama faced negative marketing and online campaigns that affected its reach. In an interview with India Today, Mahobiya claimed that the film did not get an adequate opportunity to reach audiences and suggested that an upcoming big-budget film based on the same epic may have influenced the online narrative. However, he stopped short of naming any project or filmmaker and said he could not confirm the information.

Speaking about the film’s reception, Mahobiya said, “It was negative marketing throughout. We never got a chance to reach our audience. The ones who watched our film really enjoyed it. But if they never got to see it, how will they even have an opinion?”

The producer further claimed that he had been told about efforts involving digital creators to discourage audiences from watching the film. He said, “From what we have been told, there are other movies on the same subject coming in, the big-budget film. As far as we know, a lot of negative marketing opportunities have been given to YouTubers, influencers and other people. They are spreading wrong information and asking people not to watch our film,” before adding, “I don’t know for sure, but that’s what we are being told.”

His comments come amid considerable attention around Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana, the upcoming two-part adaptation produced by Namit Malhotra. The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Raavan and is among the most closely watched upcoming Indian film projects. Mahobiya’s remarks, however, do not establish any connection between Ramayana and the alleged online campaigns against his film.

Mahobiya also admitted that marketing a film was a learning experience for him as a first-time producer. He said, “I have made a film for the first time, and I am new to this industry. I have no idea how to market a film after making it. We are not afraid of the loss, but we are disappointed that not many people managed to watch it. And hence, we want to release the film again.”

Maintaining that Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha offers a distinct interpretation, he added, “There is a lot of difference between your film and the other film that will arrive soon. But we are confident that, given a chance, people would have liked our film too.”

Directed by Abhishek Singh, Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha released in cinemas on September 25, 2026. The film stars Dev Sharma as Lord Ram, Anjali Arora as Goddess Sita, Sheel Verma as Laxman and Rajniesh Duggall in a pivotal role.

Following its theatrical run, the makers are now exploring the possibility of re-releasing the film in cinemas to give it another opportunity to reach audiences.

title: Ram Gopal Varma reacts to Janhvi Kapoor ‘Chuttamalle’ song deepfake row: “The smart thing would have been to concentrate on catching the perpetrator”
raw_summary:
Filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma has weighed in on the deepfake controversy involving Janhvi Kapoor and the song ‘Chuttamalle’, and the celebrity reaction that followed. Taking to X (formerly Twitter), he shared his views on how the matter has been handled.

Varma wrote, "The only thing all the celebrities succeeded in, is to publicise and thereby make crores and crores of people see the objectionable link.. The smart thing would have been to concentrate on catching the perpetrator and publicise that.. Instead what they did is to tweet and bring enormous attention to the victim's identity and the offensive content which is also a crime."

The only thing all the celebrities succeeded in , is to publicise and thereby make crores and crores of people see the objectionable link ..The smart thing would have been to concentrate on catching the perpetrator and publicise that ..Instead what they did is to tweet and bring enormous attention to the victim’s identity and the offensive content which is also a crime — Ram Gopal Varma (@RGVzoomin) October 4, 2026

In another tweet, he added, "When you can't WIN , you should JOIN …. . If you fight A I , it will ERASE you out of EXISTENCE." In essence, Varma's view is that a call for action against those spreading the AI-generated version would have been a better approach than a wave of public condemnation.

When you can’t WIN , you should JOIN …. . If you fight A I , it will ERASE you out of EXISTENCE 😔 — Ram Gopal Varma (@RGVzoomin) October 5, 2026

For the past few days, Janhvi has been at the centre of a social media storm after a deepfake AI video depicting the actress in an inappropriate manner, made from the ‘Chuttamalle’ song, began circulating on the platform. The actress penned a long note on Monday, 5 October, condemning the act and expressing her disappointment over such cybercrimes.

Janhvi has received strong support from her fans and followers. Her Devara co-star Jr NTR, with whom she featured in the ‘Chuttamalle’ song, also took to the platform to post a scathing message. He was followed by several big names from the South industry, including megastar Chiranjeevi.

The episode has brought two approaches into focus. One, reflected in the reaction of Janhvi and her supporters, is to publicly condemn deepfake abuse and stand with the victim. The other, voiced by Varma, is to prioritise tracking down and acting against the perpetrator while avoiding further spread of the content. Both positions come from the shared concern that AI misuse is a serious problem, though they differ on how best to respond.

title: Fire breaks out near the sets of Pati Patni Aur Panga and MTV Hustle 5, no casualties reported
raw_summary:
A fire broke out at Film City in Mumbai on Monday, with videos of the incident circulating on social media and raising concerns about the safety of teams working at the location. The fire reportedly broke out near the sets of Pati Patni Aur Panga and MTV Hustle 5. Both the teams have confirmed the incident and said that there were no casualties and everyone was safe.

A source from the Pati Patni Aur Panga set confirmed that the fire occurred outside the shooting area and clarified that there was no ongoing shoot at the time. “Yes, there was a fire outside the sets. There is no casualty. Nobody was shooting at the set of Pati Patni Aur Panga. There was no shoot happening,” a source told Hindustan Times.

Meanwhile, the MTV Hustle 5 team said that the grand finale shoot was underway when the fire broke out. According to the team, all the artists associated with the season were present at the sets at the time. Badshah, EPR, MC Square, Paradox and Agsy are among the artists associated with the season.

“All the artists were there. The fire happened suddenly. As of now, there are no casualties and everyone is safe,” the team told HT.

The incident also took place while singer Nikita Gandhi’s paparazzi spotting was underway at the location. A source from the Hustle team confirmed the development to the publication, saying, “Nikita Gandhi’s papping spotting was happening when this unfortunate incident happened.”

The cause of the fire has not been identified so far. The MTV Hustle 5 team also said that everyone was asked to leave the sets following the incident. “As soon as this happened, everybody left the sets for now. We also don’t know as of yet what was the cause behind the fire, but good thing, that everyone is safe.”

title: Sanjay Leela Bhansali and Alia Bhatt planning to revive Inshallah after Love And War: REPORT
raw_summary:
Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s Inshallah was among the films that generated considerable interest when it was announced in 2019. The project was set to feature Alia Bhatt and Salman Khan in the lead roles, marking Bhansali’s collaboration with both actors. However, the film was eventually shelved after Salman Khan reportedly opted out of the project shortly before the shoot was scheduled to begin.

Bhansali subsequently moved ahead with Gangubai Kathiawadi, starring Alia Bhatt. The film went on to receive critical recognition, with Alia winning the National Award for Best Actress for her performance. The filmmaker and actress are now collaborating once again on Love And War, which also stars Ranbir Kapoor and Vicky Kaushal.

According to a report in Mid-day, Bhansali and Alia may reunite for Inshallah once Love And War is released. However, the report suggests that the project is not being considered as a continuation of the exact version announced in 2019. While the basic storyline is expected to remain intact, the material is reportedly being reworked, with the makers planning to bring a fresh approach to the film.

Shah Rukh Khan’s Name Linked to Inshallah

Earlier this year, there was speculation that Shah Rukh Khan could potentially take over the male lead in Inshallah. However, according to the source quoted in the report, no casting decisions have been finalised yet, as Bhansali is expected to lock the script first.

The source said, “No casting gets locked on a Bhansali film without the script being finalised. Salman is occupied with Raj-DK’s film while Shah Rukh hasn’t decided his next after King. It’s also possible that the story will seek a younger actor.”

This leaves the casting of Inshallah open-ended, with the final decision reportedly depending on the direction of the reworked script. Whether Salman Khan, Shah Rukh Khan or a younger actor eventually joins Alia remains to be seen.

Meanwhile, Love And War brings together Alia Bhatt, Ranbir Kapoor and Vicky Kaushal in the lead roles. The makers recently unveiled the character posters featuring the three actors. The film, which was earlier scheduled to release this year, is now slated to arrive in theatres on January 21, 2026.

title: Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal starrer Tu Hai Meri Kiran trailer to be unveiled on October 6
raw_summary:
The wait for Tu Hai Meri Kiran is set to get more interesting as the trailer of the upcoming romantic thriller will be unveiled tomorrow. Starring real-life couple Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal, the film is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on October 23, 2026.

The upcoming film brings together romance, mystery and suspense, while keeping its central storyline largely under wraps. The trailer is expected to offer a closer look at the characters played by Sonakshi and Zaheer and provide more clues about the mystery at the heart of the story. Sonakshi Sinha and Zaheer Iqbal explore love and obsession The first look of Tu Hai Meri Kiran was unveiled on October 1. The poster introduced the film with the tagline, “She found a connection, he found an obsession.” Sharing the first look, Sonakshi also posed a question to audiences: “Where would you draw the line between LOVE and OBSESSION?”

The poster features Sonakshi and Zaheer in what appears to be a restaurant setting, hinting at a relationship that could take a darker turn. While the makers have revealed the film’s romantic thriller genre, the larger details of the plot have been kept under wraps.

 

View this post on Instagram

  A post shared by Sonakshi Sinha (@aslisona)

The trailer, arriving tomorrow, is expected to shed more light on their characters and the dynamics between them without giving away the central mystery.

Tu Hai Meri Kiran marks Sonakshi and Zaheer’s first film as a lead pair since their wedding in June 2024. The actors had previously shared screen space in the 2022 film Double XL, which also starred Huma Qureshi. They have also appeared together in the music video ‘Blockbuster.’ Karan Rawal makes feature directorial debut Written and directed by Karan Rawal, Tu Hai Meri Kiran marks his feature directorial debut. Rawal previously directed the short film Half Full and has also worked as an assistant director on projects including The Dirty Picture and Veere Di Wedding. The film is produced by Vishal Rana and others under Echelon Productions, in association with PAM Studios and AND Productions.

The title Tu Hai Meri Kiran also carries a connection to the 1993 psychological thriller Darr, which starred Shah Rukh Khan, Sunny Deol and Juhi Chawla. Juhi’s character in the film was named Kiran, while the song “Tu Hai Meri Kiran” became closely associated with the story’s theme of obsessive love.

title: Rakul Preet Singh BREAKS silence on Income Tax searches, DENIES involvement in illegal foreign remittances: "Have been paying my due taxes since the age of 20"
raw_summary:
Actress Rakul Preet Singh has broken her silence following reports about Income Tax Department searches carried out in Mumbai in connection with an ongoing probe into suspected financial irregularities in the film industry. In her first statement on the matter, Rakul has denied any involvement in illegal foreign remittances and said that the search was not related to her.

Rakul Preet Singh denies involvement Addressing the reports, Rakul said that she wanted to clarify her position and objected to what she described as unverified and sensationalised coverage. “It’s heartbreaking to see that there’s a growing trend amongst the self styled online reporters & some mainstream media journalists to sensationalise the news without verifying facts,” she said.

Rakul went on to specifically deny that she was involved in the alleged financial irregularities. “The search was not pertaining to me,” she said, adding that she comes from an Armed Forces background and entered the film industry without a godfather. The actress also stated that she has been paying her taxes since the age of 20 and described herself as a responsible, law-abiding citizen. “I am not involved in any kind of illegal foreign remittance in personal capacity or on behalf of any Production house,” Rakul said. Rakul Preet Singh DENIES holding benami property Rakul also addressed speculation surrounding alleged undisclosed assets. She said that she does not hold any benami property for anyone in India or abroad. “I would also add here that I do not hold any Benami property on behalf of anyone anywhere in the country or abroad,” she said. The actress further stated that nobody had ever gifted her any property and that she does not accept expensive gifts as a matter of principle. Rakul urges media outlets to retract reports Rakul concluded her statement by calling on publications and individuals who, according to her, had published inaccurate reports to retract them and clarify the facts. “I urge all those who published these false, malicious and speculative reports to retract them and clarify the facts,” she said.

Acknowledging the commercial pressures faced by media organisations, Rakul said that such pressures should not come at the expense of accuracy or an individual's reputation. “I understand that everyone running a media business however big has their own commercial pressures. But it cannot come at the cost of facts. And certainly not at the cost of someone’s reputation and livelihood,” she added.

 

View this post on Instagram

  A post shared by Rakul Singh (@rakulpreet)

On September 28, the Mumbai Income Tax Department conducted searches at around 12 locations reportedly linked to Rakul, her father-in-law and producer Vashu Bhagnani, and Panorama Studios, associated with producer Kumar Mangat Pathak. The searches were reportedly part of an investigation into suspected irregularities involving film financing and overseas transactions.

Reports had said that officials were examining documents, bank records and financial transactions as part of the probe. The focus was reportedly on substantial funds allegedly remitted overseas under the stated heads of shooting expenses, production costs and overseas distribution. However, no specific amount, formal finding or charge has been publicly announced by the authorities. A search by an investigative agency does not by itself establish wrongdoing, and the investigation remains ongoing.

title: R. Madhavan set to host Game Changers featuring startup founders and global investors; details inside!
raw_summary:
Optimystix Entertainment India Limited has announced Game Changers, a new original business reality format that will be hosted by actor and filmmaker R. Madhavan. The show will be produced in Dubai for the Middle East market, with plans to explore its expansion to other territories.

Game Changers will bring together startup founders from different parts of the world, giving them an opportunity to pitch their businesses before an international panel of investors. The investor panel will feature representatives from Dubai, London, Russia and the United States.

Production on the show is scheduled to begin shortly. The format will focus on entrepreneurship, business decisions and the personal journeys behind companies as founders attempt to secure investment and scale their ventures.

Vipul D Shah, Founder and Chairman of Optimystix, said the company sees the project as more than a standalone television show. “Game Changers is being developed as a future-facing global entertainment franchise for Optimystix. It is more than a new show. It is an owned IP with the potential to travel across markets, attract marquee brand partnerships and create multiple monetisation streams over time,” he said.

He added, “We are combining our proven expertise in creating mass-audience entertainment with a format that speaks directly to the global energy around entrepreneurship, innovation and investment.”

According to Rajesh Bahl, Co-Founder and Group CEO of Optimystix, the format will also explore the people and decisions behind the businesses being presented. “The format goes beyond a conventional pitch show. It spotlights the ambition, resilience, strategy and personal conviction behind promising businesses while giving audiences an inside view of what it takes to build, fund and scale a company in today’s competitive global economy,” he said.

Dubai has been chosen as the production base for the first edition. The city’s position as an international business hub is expected to provide the show with access to founders, investors and businesses from different markets. The UAE edition could also pave the way for regional versions and adaptations of the format in the future.

With R. Madhavan as host, the show will combine the business-focused format with a mainstream entertainment element. His role is expected to involve engaging with the participating founders and taking audiences through their journeys as they pitch their ventures to the investor panel.

For Optimystix, Game Changers marks a move towards developing and owning original formats alongside its existing work across television, films, OTT and digital content. The company has produced more than 160 television shows over the past two decades, including Comedy Circus, Crime Patrol, Baalveer, Rising Star and Laughter Chefs. Its film credits include OMG 2, Khel Khel Mein and The Diplomat.

With Game Changers, the production house is looking to build an original format around the growing interest in startups, entrepreneurship and investment, while using Dubai as the starting point for its international ambitions.

title: Janhvi Kapoor condemns morphed AI video from Devara Part 1 song ‘Chuttumalle’: “Consent, choice and respect for a woman's body should be basic”
raw_summary:
Janhvi Kapoor has spoken out against the circulation of a morphed AI-generated video featuring her from the Devara Part 1 song ‘Chuttumalle’. The incident has sparked widespread concern on social media, with the actress once again becoming a victim of digital manipulation. Janhvi, who has previously spoken about being targeted by deepfake technology, took to Instagram to condemn the misuse of technology and the violation of women’s consent.

In a detailed note, Janhvi highlighted how the objectification of women through manipulated digital content has become an increasingly serious concern. She wrote, “The criminal misuse of technology to objectify women and circulate fictionalised content without consent is deeply violating, bordering on sexual assault. Almost every woman in my industry has faced some version of this, and women everywhere are increasingly being subjected to it,” her note read and continued, “Consent, choice and respect for a woman's body should be among the most basic notions of humanity. Yet somehow, they continue to be treated as complicated. They are not.”

Janhvi further explained that consent cannot be assumed or taken for granted under any circumstances. Drawing an analogy, she wrote, “It is surprising that it still seems too nuanced for some people to understand that even if a woman says yes five days in a row and no on the sixth, that no must be respected. If she happens to wear a miniskirt, it does not give anyone permission to put a camera up her skirt, capture violating angles or visually exploit her body. What a woman is comfortable with, where she draws the line and what she chooses to do with her body are decisions that belong exclusively to her. This is basic.”

The actress also placed the incident within the larger conversation around women’s safety, saying that the threat of violation has now extended into the digital space. “This goes far beyond the ai videos I have dealt with over the last few days, or anything I have personally experienced throughout my career. It is about the larger reality of being a woman, the gaze, the judgement, the constant negotiation for safety, and the feeling that our boundaries somehow remain open to interpretation. That threat has now expanded into the digital sphere, when we have not even adequately addressed the very real, physical fear that continues to disrupt the lives of women every day,” she said.

Janhvi also stressed that the responsibility cannot solely be placed on women to protect themselves - “The answer cannot simply be to "protect your daughter." we also need to undo the conditioning that makes people believe they are entitled to violate somebody else's boundaries in the first place. And part of that change will come from exemplary men with the moral compass and the spine to say clearly what is right and what is wrong.”

The actress thanked her Devara co-star NTR Jr., along with Chiranjeevi, Vijay Deverakonda and Khushbu Sundar, for speaking up against the incident and supporting her. She expressed, “I am deeply touched by NTR sir for taking such a strong stand and condemning this violation. Thank you, sir. When someone whom millions look up to speaks up about something that may not directly concern him, it makes a difference to every woman who has experienced some degree of this behaviour.” “Thank you also to Chiranjeevi sir, Vijay and Khushbu ma'am for amplifying that sentiment and calling for action against this mentality and these immoral practices,” she added.

She concluded by urging people to reconsider the attitude towards women’s boundaries and choice, “I hope everything unfolding around us right now forces those who participate in any form of harassment to introspect. Is it really too much for a woman to ask to simply be treated and seen as a human being? Her body. Her image. Her boundaries. Her choice.”

title: EXCLUSIVE: Siddharth P Malhotra reveals Ikka sequel and Shaque Season 2 are in the works; also shares happiness at the response to Parineeti Chopra starrer show: “Haven’t got so many calls for a series before”
raw_summary:
Filmmaker and producer Siddharth P Malhotra has had a good 2026. His Netflix film Ikka, starring Sunny Deol and Akshaye Khanna, grabbed a lot of eyeballs earlier this year. Now, his web show Shaque: Trust No One on the same platform has been doing well too.

In an exclusive chat with Bollywood Hungama, Malhotra revealed that both the projects will have a second part. “Ikka has broken records. There is Ikka 2 being worked on. Shaque has now broken records and Shaque Season 2 is being done. It has been a great year. Shaque Season 2 won’t continue the same story. It will be a new story. But a season 2 is in the works. We are writing it,” he said.

Malhotra also shared that director Rensil D’Silva had earlier envisioned Shaque as a movie when he came up with the idea years ago. “It was a story Rensil had cracked about 8-9 years ago,” he said. “Initially, it was a feature film. Then we worked on it and we said that let’s see if we can make it into series. After writing it as a series, we realized that it has legs and potential. Then I sold it to Netflix. They liked the idea.”

Malhotra is happy with the response the show has generated in little over a week. “We have been getting a lot of feedback. It’s done really well. Even after one week, it’s at number one. In my whole career, I haven’t got so many calls for a series. Even people from South Bombay are calling and saying that they binged and enjoyed it. It’s a good feeling. Netflix is very happy. It’s done very well for them. It’s in the top 10 in 20-30 countries. When you go into a party or function, people are willingly saying that they found it very good. They will say it saamne se only when they actually liked it. If they didn’t, they would say that they haven’t watched it yet,” he said.

Shaque is a whodunit where the identity of the culprit is revealed at the end. In today’s times of social media, there is every chance of someone or the other revealing the climax. Malhotra said that one can’t control that. “Social media is good and bad. If somebody wants to reveal the climax, you can’t stop that person. As far as people are talking and commenting about the show, we are very happy. Now, even after revealing the climax, if people are still watching the show, it’s the writing team’s victory,” he said.

During the trailer launch of Shaque, lead actor Parineeti Chopra shared that she came to know after starting the shoot that she is pregnant. Hence, the makers ensured that she stayed at the same place where they were shooting, so that she doesn’t have to travel. Malhotra said that this wasn’t challenging for them. “It is the responsibility between Sapna (Malhotra) and me to take care of her. She could have said that she is pregnant and she won’t be able to shoot. But she is continued the shoot. So, we should take care of her, respect her and do the best we can,” he said.

As a director, Siddharth P Malhotra has made films on varied subjects like We Are Family (2010), Hichki (2018), Tribhanga (2021), Maharaj (2024) and Ikka (2026). When asked whether it has always been a conscious decision for him not to repeat genres, he said, “It’s not a conscious effort to not repeat a genre. It’s actually an effort to try and find a story I can resonate to. Actually, for me the genre is the same as they are all (stories of) human relationships. The worlds might be different but the stories are of human relations and complex situations.”

Malhotra has had a successful and long collaboration with Netflix with a series of projects like Tribhanga, Maharaj, Ikka and now Shaque. “I have known Monika (Shergill, Vice President, Content) from the time I did Sanjivani (TV show) and before that. Their team is very co-operative and collaborative. All the success of any show or film of Netflix is a collaborative effort. Their names don’t appear but they put in a lot of hard work. No single person can take credit of a success. It’s always a team work. Netflix has been a great collaborator and we are collaborating a lot now,” he said.
